sections.h2: Campbell County offices and who sets the rate
sections.html:
Three offices share a Campbell bill. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value, the Sheriff's Office mails and collects, and the County Clerk inherits what goes delinquent. Rates come from neither the PVA nor the sheriff: each taxing district's board figures its rate from the assessments inside that district.

The county runs along the Ohio and Licking Rivers and has two seats, Newport and Alexandria, with sheriff's windows in each. By law the PVA assesses at 100 percent of fair market value, meaning the price a willing buyer and seller would agree on. Field staff look at every parcel in person at least every four years, and new construction is reviewed when it appears. Which of the county's school districts serves a house changes the school line on the bill.

Rates move each year under House Bill 44. A district can take the compensating rate, which keeps revenue from existing property flat as values rise, or a rate that raises up to 4 percent more, which needs a public hearing. A rate above that can be put to a recall vote. A rise in your assessed value therefore does not automatically mean a bigger bill.

Finished bills reach the sheriff by September 15, and mailing usually follows around November 1. The discount phase runs from November 1 through November 30, with payment before December 1 earning the discount.

Campbell County payment calendar
Payment periodAmount owed
NovemberFace amount less 2%
DecemberFace amount, no discount
JanuaryDelinquent, plus 5 percent
From February 1Plus 10 percent and a 10 percent sheriff's add-on fee
Older yearsSettled at the County Clerk, never the sheriff

One line item surprises owners: the 911 fee printed on the bill is exempt from the 2% discount and stays at full price. The sheriff mails only to the listed owner and cannot redirect a bill to a lender, so anyone with escrow should pass the bill along at once.

sections.h2: How to pay the Campbell sheriff
sections.html:
You can pay on the web, by mail, or in person at either sheriff's window. The Newport window is inside the County Administration Building, 1098 Monmouth Street. The Alexandria window is at 8330 West Main Street. Each is open weekdays, 8 in the morning to 4 in the afternoon.

An outside vendor runs the web payment page. Cards carry a 3 percent charge paid by the cardholder, e-checks cost $3, and e-checks over $30,000 are refused. None of that money goes to the sheriff. For a check by mail, make it out to the sheriff, write the bill number on it, and treat the canceled check as your receipt.

Should a check come back, the bill returns to unpaid status in both the sheriff's and PVA's records, and you must repay on the schedule printed on the bill. During a closing week, a bounced check can leave a lien open.

sections.h2: How a Campbell County appeal works
sections.html:
A PVA conference has to happen before the 13-day inspection period ends, and the appeal itself is filed with the county. Inspection starts the first Monday in May, and the Board of Assessment Appeals then meets for five days starting 25 to 35 days after it closes.

The filing deadline is the workday after inspection ends, but read the dates on your notice and get the exact last day from the PVA before filing. Anyone paid to represent you must be an attorney, appraiser, accountant, broker or similar professional under KRS 133.120.

Good evidence for a Newport or Alexandria house includes recent sales of similar homes, photos of damage and repair estimates. Ask the PVA for the list of sales used to value your home, and request it first.

Owners who reach 65, or who are totally disabled, can apply for a homestead or disability exemption through the PVA, which can state the filing cutoff for the year. Disability verification is due before December 31. If you are turning 65, contact the PVA before paying.

The PVA at 1098 Monmouth Street, (859) 292-3871, also fixes a wrong property address, mailing address or owner name. Corrections can be written on the return stub, which the sheriff forwards. An assessment or exemption can be changed only by the PVA.

  • PVA, 1098 Monmouth Street: value, address, name and exemption questions.
  • Sheriff, Newport or Alexandria: bill lookup and payment.
  • County Clerk, (859) 292-3845: any year that has gone delinquent.

Farm acreage is valued at its agricultural value, which can sit far below the market price per acre in urban areas. A seller with a few acres at the edge of Alexandria should ask the PVA how the parcel is classed.

Each line on the bill belongs to a different taxing district, and the district's own board set its rate. If a line looks wrong, ask who controls it. The PVA answers questions about the value the rates are applied to, as well as a wrong name or address. The sheriff can explain the amount due and the payment dates. Neither office can change a rate.

Keep an eye on the 911 line, which does not get the 2% discount. A buyer's agent comparing two houses should look at the total on the bill, not just the assessed value.

sections.h2: What happens to the taxes when you sell
sections.html:
The debt follows the parcel. Before closing, the title company will ask for a payoff of the current bill and of any delinquent certificate. KRS 134.015 makes the tax a personal debt of the owner on the January 1 assessment date, and the delinquency lien continues under KRS 134.420 no matter who owns the house afterward.

A bill that outlasts the sheriff's season moves to the County Clerk carrying a 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's fee and 1 percent monthly interest. Clerk, county attorney and third-party purchaser fees pile on from there. The clerk at (859) 292-3845 gives the live figure.

Falling behind does not block a sale. You can still sell as-is and let the payoff come out of the proceeds, and early numbers from the clerk show what remains.

Values are high in Campbell County. The 2020 to 2024 median for an owner-occupied home is $252,000, and 182 building permits were issued in 2025. The county is part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area, with 95,441 residents in 2025 and 43,090 homes counted in mid-2025. Owners live in 71.1 percent of homes. Typical rent is $1,145 a month, and typical owner cost with a mortgage is $1,627.

About 86.1 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, which points to more moves and more rentals. Owners of older Newport homes, duplexes or inherited houses can sell directly for cash when repairs or tenants slow a standard listing.

sections.h2: Before you list a Campbell County house
sections.html:
1. Call the PVA at (859) 292-3871 to confirm the value, address, owner name and any exemption on the account.
  2. Ask the sheriff in Newport or Alexandria for the current bill and whether it has been paid.
  3. Call the County Clerk at (859) 292-3845 about any delinquent year.
  4. Hand the payoff amounts to the title company so the closing agent can settle them from your proceeds.

Doing these early means corrections can be made on the return stub or at the PVA before a contract is signed.

faqs.q: When do Campbell County tax bills go out?
faqs.a: Mailing typically happens around November 1. The 2% discount lasts through November 30, December is face value, January adds 5%, and after January 31 a 10% penalty and sheriff's fee apply.

faqs.q: Where do I take a Campbell County payment?
faqs.a: Visit the Sheriff's Office in Newport (1098 Monmouth Street) or Alexandria (8330 West Main Street), mail it, or use the vendor link on the sheriff's tax page.
No. The 911 line on a bill is outside the 2% discount.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about my Campbell value?
faqs.a: The PVA, at (859) 292-3871. The sheriff only collects, and cannot alter an assessment, address or exemption.

faqs.q: Can a house with unpaid Campbell taxes still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent bills sit with the County Clerk, and closing pays them from the proceeds. Ask the clerk, at (859) 292-3845, for the amount before fixing a date.
